jobs.title: Career Coach at The Centers
jobs.description: Employer: The Centers Expires: 11/26/2026 About the RoleThe Career Coach assists individuals in developing job readiness by assessing a job seeker's knowledge, skills and interests in order to steer him/her to an appropriate career path and successful job placement. Coach's work one-on-one with job seekers, virtually and in-person, to assess barriers to employment, completes an Individual Service Plan, and generate internal and external referrals to remove or mitigate barriers to employment. Coaches and develops job seekers job search skills, including formulating resumes, researching job openings, applying for positions and preparing for interviews. Assists Instructors by participating in weekly assigned workshops. Offers networking opportunities to Job Seekers with perspective employers.This position will work in-person Monday-Friday from 8:00am-4:30pm or 8:30am-5:00pm, with some evenings. This is not a remote position.Job QualificationsHigh School Diploma or equivalent with 4 years of experience in workforce required.Bachelor's degree in related area preferred.Minimum 1 year of relevant exposure to or experience working with job seekers experiencing challenges in finding employment. Experience in a related field such as workforce development or social services is preferred.Proficient in using working with electronic platforms (i.e. Microsoft software Office Suite, internet research, database managements, and virtual learning platforms). Requires travel to other facilities and meetings as needed. Reliable transportation is required, a valid driver's license and personal vehicle strongly preferred.Availability to work outside of standard business hours, including evenings and weekends to accommodate program requirements and client needs, as well as participation on trainings and meetings.Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish both oral and written is required.Essential Job Duties & ResponsibilitiesConduct interviews with job seekers to assess barriers to employment and fill out individual service plans to lead to successful job placement.Assist job seekers with referral information and follows up regularly on the progress being made to resolve barriers to employment.Provide emergency assistance and referral to other programs or agencies as needed.Responsible for monitoring attendance and case note reporting through database management system.Responsible for updating and maintaining job seeker files with the highest level of detail and timeliness possible. Ensure that all required forms are properly completed.Maintain current and organized information on job postings in the Greater Cleveland area.Meet with job seekers on a daily basis, provide them with effective job leads, perform any and all activities conducive to the job seeker's obtaining employment, and following up on job search activities.Revise and correct any and all documentation produced by job seekers to ensure quality material, such as resumes and cover letters.Responsible for attending and leading or assisting with assigned workshops. Ensures alternative coverage is found or communicated to Instruction team to assist with alternative coverage.Working with the Job Developer, develops and maintains cordial relationships with current and potential employers and all El Barrio stakeholders.Assist with hiring events and ensure attendance of job seekers.Maintain contact with employed participants to ensure personal and family stability and job retention.Ensures all data and records are accurate and current utilizing the appropriate database systems and paper records.Willingness and ability to work virtually and on-site with job seekersActively working towards accomplishing and meeting program goals as outlined within contracts, while keeping the job seeker at the front of mind.Assists with Workforce projectsOther duties as assignedAbout The CentersThe Centers through healing, teaching, and inspiring helps individuals and families to reach their full potential. We provide health, family, and workforce services at 11 locations throughout Greater Cleveland, creating life-changing solutions for people to lead healthier and more successful lives. We strive to be a service-oriented workplace that pioneers and co-creates solutions while fostering an inclusive community where our team members thrive.Our Workforce Center impacts local communities through the linkage of underserved job seekers with local employers through our culturally competent job readiness training, case management, national third party certifications, job placements and retention support with a large network of corporate partners. Through our training tracks in Customer Service, Hospitality, Pharmacy, and general job readiness in both English and Spanish, we are able to provide essential skills to our job seekers and to help prepare them for success in today's workplace.Wellbeing and BenefitsProviding quality benefits to our staff is important to us. Just as important is our staff's well-being. That's why we offer a number of choices from medical to dental to vision plans to meet the different needs of our staff.Choice of medical and dental plansHealth Savings AccountFlexible Spending Account for Health and Dependent CareVisionSupport for continuing education and credential renewalLife InsuranceRetirement Savings (401k) with a company contributionMental Health SupportEmployee Assistance ProgramCalm SubscriptionShort and Long term DisabilityThe Centers is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Supervising Mental Health Clinician (New York) (LMHC or LCSW) at MindView Therapy
jobs.description: Employer: MindView Therapy Expires: 11/26/2026 MindView Therapy is an outpatient group providing evidence-based care to adult clients. We give early-career clinicians the structure, supervision, and technology to grow into confident, licensed professionals. We are measurement-based and progress-driven. Care is structured, outcomes are tracked, and clinical decisions are informed by data rather than guesswork. We are also building a real community of clinicians who grow together. Peer consultation, shared learning, and genuine collegiality are part of how we practice, not an afterthought. Position Overview:You will deliver telehealth psychotherapy to an adult caseload while practicing under a New York LMHC or LCSW license. We will also train you as a clinical supervisor, and you will supervise a small team of limited permit clinicians. Scheduling, intake, and insurance billing are handled by our operations team so you can focus on clinical work. Core Duties:Carry a caseload of 25 video sessions per week once your caseload ramps (ramp takes 2–3 months).Supervise 5 limited permit (LP) clinicians, 1 hour per week each.Total commitment of 30 direct hours per week (clinical sessions plus supervision).Complete diagnostic intakes, treatment plans, and progress notes within 24 hours.Deliver CBT, ACT, ERP, CPT, and other evidence-based interventions. Training and Supervision:6-week dual-track training in foundations and documentation.Supervisor training to prepare you to lead and develop LP clinicians.Robust onboarding and ongoing training in evidence-based modalities and measurement-based care.Weekly individual supervision plus a small peer consultation group.Continuous skills training at no cost to you (supervision and training equivalent to $14,000 market value, provided free of charge). Minimum Requirements:New York License in Mental Health Counseling or Clinical Social Work.Private, secure work-from-home space with reliable high-speed internet.Ability to pass NY OMH background screening. ***Only accepting Licensed Mental Health Counselors or Clinical Social Workers who are able to obtain or already have their full license in the state of New York.*** Preferred Qualifications:Fluency in an additional language (Spanish, Russian, Mandarin, Bengali, ASL).Prior supervision or mentoring experience. Compensation:Initially $60 per session. Bonus of $5 per client seen over 25 per week.Salaried position at $103,000 per year. Benefits (upon full caseload):401kHealth insurancePaid time off Schedule and Work Style:Telehealth only. Treat clients located anywhere in New York State.Single weekend day availability preferred.Visit us at mindviewtherapy.com Benefits:401(k)Health insurancePaid time off

jobs.title: Extended Day Teacher at City of Cambridge, MA
jobs.description: Employer: City of Cambridge, MA Expires: 11/26/2026 POSITION SUMMARY:The Extended Day Teacher develops and leads a safe, engaging, inclusive, and developmentally responsive after-school program for elementary-aged children within the King Open Extended Day program. The position is responsible for planning and implementing enrichment-based curriculum and activities that support children's social, emotional, physical, and academic growth while fostering meaningful connections between school-day and after-school experiences. The Extended Day Teacher collaborates closely with families, school-day staff, program staff, and community partners to support student success and maintain a positive, child-centered learning environment. This position also provides supervision and guidance to assistant staff, interns, and volunteers and participates in school-day classroom support activities during the academic day.ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES:The essential functions or duties listed below are intended only as illustrations of the various type of work that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position.Lead and develop a child-centered, welcoming, inclusive, and richly diverse after-school classroom serving mixed-grade elementary students.Plan and implement an engaging, well-rounded, developmentally responsive, hands-on after-school curriculum that promotes children's social, emotional, physical, and academic development; regularly incorporates gym games, team-building, arts and crafts, and social-emotional learning; reflect school-day experiences; include at least three 6-week Project-Based Learning units over the school year on themes such as physical recreation, performing arts, visual arts, science, and ecology; and intentionally link with school-day learning by coordinating with teachers to align projects, share relevant student insights, and reinforce key skills and routines across settings.Supervise at least one part-time assistant and, as needed, coordinate and supervise support teachers, inclusion staff, high school interns, and volunteers; participate in interviewing and training new assistants, interns, and volunteers.Participate in at least five (5) hours per week of in-class work in King Open School's school-day classrooms to support students and teachers during the academic day, including one-on-one support of children, assisting King Open faculty in curriculum delivery and differentiated instruction, small group facilitation, and participatory observation.Participate in school-day support meetings such as IEP meetings or family conferences and engage families in a consistent partnership in the education of children, including regularly facilitating family engagement events.Maintain a "child growth portfolio" for each child in the King Open Extended Day classroom each school year, including ongoing documentation of child progress, daily activities, outreach, and staff meetings, as well as regular weekly scheduling and lesson planning.Manage the classroom budget, including ordering supplies and snacks, planning and leading field trips, and engaging outside consultants and vendors.Maintain professional integrity and conduct by following and promoting program policies, procedures, and routines; collaborate and maintain links to King Open Extended Day staff, school-day staff, outside service providers, supervisors, and families; and during the school year, assist families with referrals, applications, and placement into DHSP summer programs—coordinating with program staff and the central office as neededPerform other duties as required.Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.QUALIFICATIONS: Education/ExperienceHigh school diploma or equivalent required; associate's or bachelor's degree in child/youth development, education, social work, or a related human service field strongly preferred.Three (3) years of relevant experience with school-aged children (Kindergarten through 5th grade), including direct work in educational, after-school, youth development, or recreation settings; early childhood experience may be considered if clearly transferable to school-aged groups. Preferred experience includes after-school programming, preschool settings, urban youth, public schools, and/or mental health services.Staff supervision experience strongly preferred.Bilingual or bicultural background is a plus.Knowledge of the Nurtured Heart Approach and/or Responsive Classroom techniques is a plus.An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.Knowledge, Skills, and AbilitiesCommitment to the social and developmental benefits of after-school work for children.Dedication to the importance and benefits of connections between after-school and school-day experiences for children.Strong written and verbal communication skills.Sense of humor and ability to serve as a strong, positive role model.Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and follow-through on multiple projects.Experience working with families from diverse cultural, ethnic, linguistic, and socioeconomic backgrounds, providing outreach and facilitating communication and strong relationships.Experience in and commitment to a collaborative, team-oriented environment.Commitment to anti-bias and culturally proficient practices.Commitment to enhancing reflective practice and to accepting and providing supervision and guidance.Commitment to continuous improvement in service quality and to the program's mission.Proficiency with Microsoft Office or a comparable system, as well as computer- and internet-based lesson planning, is preferred.Ability to work and interact effectively with individuals and groups across diverse identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies.SUPERVISION RECEIVED:Works under the general supervision of the Site Director (King Open Extended Day) within the Department of Human Service Programs and exercises independent judgment within established policies, seeking guidance on unusual or complex situations.SUPERVISION EXERCISED:Provides supervision to part-time assistant teachers and interns; delivers daily direction, scheduling support, and coaching to ensure high-quality, developmentally appropriate programming.WORK ENVIRONMENT:Work is performed in classrooms, on outdoor playgrounds, and during occasional field trips; noise levels range from moderate to very loud.PHYSICAL DEMANDS:The employee is occasionally required to run during play or in response to an emergency and to lift and/or move a child, and visual acuity is required for child supervision. Employees are frequently required to engage with children on the floor and at their eye level, using their hands and arms to handle and manipulate objects and to reach.REQUIRED DOCUMENTS:ResumeCover LetterThe City of Cambridge's workforce, like the community it serves, is diverse. Applicants must have the ability to work and interact effectively with individuals and groups with a variety of identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies.

jobs.description: Employer: State of Connecticut Executive Branch Expires: 11/26/2026 Transportation Planner 2 (40 Hour)Office of Rail, Capital Planning UnitRecruitment #261030-8876FE-001Location Newington, CTDate Opened 11/6/2026 12:00:00 AMSalary $91,979 - $132,381/yearJob Type Open to the PublicClose Date 11/20/2026 11:59:00 PMGo Back Apply View BenefitsFacebook Share Tweet on X LinkedIn Share email sendIntroductionThe State of Connecticut Department of Transportation (CTDOT), is accepting applications for Transportation Planner 2 to join the Office of Rail, Capital Planning Unit. The Capital Planning Unit is responsible for leading and supporting statewide rail capital planning activities within the Connecticut Department of Transportation. This position develops, evaluates, and prioritizes passenger and freight rail projects, ensuring coordination across CTDOT bureaus, partner agencies, and federal programs such as FRA Corridor ID and NEC Commission initiatives. The role emphasizes multimodal integration, data-driven decision making, and alignment with the Department’s long-range strategic goals.WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOUOur State Employee Benefits Overview page!Professional growth and development opportunities.A healthy work/life balance to all employees.Working for an award winning agency! CTDOT was recently awarded the Employer of the Year award by the Connecticut Society of Civil Engineers (CSCE) and named the Women's Transportation Seminar (WTS) CT Employer of the Year for 2024!POSITION HIGHLIGHTSMonday - FridayFull Time, 40 hours per weekFirst ShiftLocation: NewingtonP-4 (Engineering and Scientific) bargaining unitThis position is eligible to apply for telework after successful completion of the working test period, and thereafter, in accordance with the Telework Policy. Employees in their working test period must work on site in the office. Learn more about the Telework Policy. THE ROLEThe Transportation Planner 2 is responsible for advanced planning and analysis of Connecticut’s passenger and freight rail capital program, supporting the development, evaluation, and prioritization of projects within CTDOT’s Office of Rail. The Transportation Planner 2 (Capital Planning) serves as a working lead and subject matter expert on rail infrastructure planning, federal program coordination, and long-range investment strategy development for rail corridors in Connecticut.Key Responsibilities include: Lead or coordinate capital planning studies, including identification, scoping, and justification of new or upgraded rail projects (stations, bridges, track, rolling stock, and yard facilities).Develop and manage planning documentation supporting the Rail Capital Program, including reports, cost estimates, schedules, phasing, and funding strategy.Assist with preparation of federal funding applications (FRA Corridor ID, FSP-NEC, BIL/IIJA grants, etc.) and coordinate with internal and external partners to ensure compliance with federal guidelines.Support multimodal planning initiatives integrating rail with highway, bus, and active transportation networks.Review consultant studies, service development plans, and feasibility analyses to align with CTDOT goals and federal requirements.Collaborate with the Project Concepts and Design units to transition projects from planning to design.Participate in coordination with Amtrak, Metro-North Railroad, FRA, FTA, NEC Commission, and regional MPOs regarding service planning, capital improvement prioritization, and funding allocations.Develop maps, reports, presentations, and data analyses illustrating rail system performance, capacity constraints, and investment opportunities.Lead or assist in maintaining the CTDOT Rail Capital Planning Database and contribute to the annual Transportation Capital Plan and Time for CT program updates.Represent the Office of Rail at interagency working groups, legislative hearings, and public information sessions.Our ideal candidate will possess the following:Considerable knowledge of transportation planning principles, practices, and federal funding programs related to rail infrastructure.Skill in project prioritization, economic and ridership analysis, and cost-benefit evaluation.Ability to interpret and apply federal guidance (e.g., FRA, FTA, NEC Commission).Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, GIS, and data visualization tools.Strong written and verbal communication skills, including preparation of technical and policy documents.Ability to coordinate multidisciplinary efforts across CTDOT bureaus, local agencies, consultants, and federal partners.Supervisory ability and experience mentoring junior planners or interns.YOUR CAREER WITH USLearn more about our Transportation PlannersABOUT USAs one of Connecticut’s largest State agencies, DOT employs approximately 3,300 individuals statewide in five bureaus. CTDOT is guided by its mission to improve lives through transportation. Our infrastructure and transit systems are essential to the safety and mobility of Connecticut residents, and our work strengthens both economic and community development. CTDOT is committed to fostering a workforce that reflects the communities it serves, and individuals with broad-ranging backgrounds and life experiences are encouraged to apply.Learn more about our mission, vision, and values!Selection PlanCheck out our Applicant Tips on How to Apply! Clients are referred from the Fairfax Juvenile and Domestic Relations District Court with diagnostically complex presentations. Clinician office may be located in the Juvenile Detention Center. Client presentations might include serious and persistent mental illness, serious emotional disturbance, at-risk issues, substance use disorders and co-occurring disorders. Client concerns might include culture and equity, socioeconomics, and health. Provides assessments specific to the needs of the youth behavioral health population, plus collaboration, monitoring, and advocacy. Candidates should be familiar with primary therapy and case management activities related to Comprehensive Services Act (CSA) requirements. Performs utilization management activities related to requirements of insurance companies and Medicaid manual requirements for case management and therapeutic services. Manages a caseload in accordance with utilization guidelines to ensure smooth client service flow from entry to intake through discharge from services, to minimize service wait for clients at each stage of treatment. Adapts and modifies clinical treatment approaches to clinical complexity and mental health status. The clinician will monitor treatment planning and progress and maintain detailed clinical charts and confidentiality. Will use collaborative documentation to enter clinical services notes. Adheres to established business license related billing procedures according to insurance, local, state, and federal standards, regulations and statutes. Serves as a clinical expert for youth behavioral health services and collaborate with JDRDC program personnel accordingly. The clinician may have the opportunity to serve as a licensure supervisor to staff or student interns, or to directly supervise/ authorize services provided by unlicensed staff. Rewarding Careers video.Illustrative Duties(The illustrative duties listed in this specification are representative of the class but are not an all-inclusive list. implements therapeutic treatment plans;Recommends, monitors, and coordinates clinical care to non-Community Services Board clients;Consults with professionals on a variety of problems including delivery of needed services for clinically complex cases;Provides liaison to community agencies to facilitate communication and service provision for clients requiring multiple services;Monitors and analyzes the impact of psychotropic medication on client's functioning and mental status;Provides risk assessments for dangerousness to self and others;Provides crisis stabilization and crisis management.Required Knowledge Skills and Abilities(The knowledge, skills and abilities listed in this specification are representative of the class but are not an all-inclusive list.)Extensive techniques;Thorough knowledge of major schools of treatment of emotionally and socially disturbed individuals;Knowledge of psychiatric, psychological, and/or sociological terminology and concepts;Ability to conduct mental health assessments and apply treatment approaches/modalities;Ability to formulate diagnoses for clients with acute, chronic, severe mental illness;Ability to diagnostically interpret data obtained from psychological test results, social histories, and interviews;Ability to develop and maintain effective working relationships with co-workers, public and private sector organizations, community groups, and the general public;Ability to monitor and analyze the impact of psychotropic medications;Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing.Employment StandardsMINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:Graduation from an accredited college with a master's degree in social work, psychology, counseling, or nursing; plus two years of clinical experience. CERTIFICATES AND LICENSES REQUIRED:Possession of a current license to practice in the Commonwealth of Virginia in one of the following:Licensed Clinical Social Worker,Licensed Professional Counselor,Clinical Psychologist,Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist, Licensed Substance Abuse Treatment Practitioner orLicensed Nurse Practitioner (LNP).CPR/First Aid certifications (with 3 months of hire)NECESSARY SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS:The appointee to this position will be required to complete a criminal background check, a Child Protective Services Registry check, and sanction screening to the satisfaction of the employer. jobs.title: Chief Academic Officer (#5277) at Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit
jobs.description: Employer: Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit Expires: 11/26/2026 Chief Academic Officer:Milton, PA The Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit (CSIU) is seeking to hire a Chief Academic Officer (CAO). This position is responsible for the effective and efficient operation of the teaching, leadership, and learning functions of the intermediate unit. These functions include the academic, instructional, curricular, professional learning, assessment, instructional technology, leadership, school improvement, and leadership development. Functions also include PDE initiatives and requirements for all age levels and facets of the educational experience, both school-based and community-based, supported by the intermediate unit, with an emphasis on Early Childhood through Grade 12. The CAO serves as the liaison between the member school districts, technical schools, colleges, the community and the intermediate unit in supporting the teaching and learning functions of the CSIU. Essential responsibilities for program and service areas include but are not limited to the following:Curriculum, Instruction and Assessment ServicesSchool-Age ServicesLeadership Development Salary Range: $150,000 - $165,000 dependent on experience and credentials. This is an exempt middle management position working 260 days per year. This position includes a strong benefits package consisting of medical, dental, vision and life insurance; retirement options through Pennsylvania Public School Employees Retirement System (PSERS). CYP provides appropriate developmental care and instruction for children and youth ranging in age from six weeks to 18 years. The incumbent is responsible for administration of the facility to include assisting the CDC Director with budgeting and financial management, personnel management, food service, facility operations, and compliance, among other tasks. The incumbent serves as a first level supervisor for assigned staff and assists the CDC Director in the supervision of the day-to-day operation of the program/activity. The incumbent reports and works directly with the CDC Director with minimum supervision to accomplish the overall objectives of administering the program. Work is subject to review for adequacy of program accomplishments, effectiveness, and compatibility with other work, and compliance with requirements. The incumbent is responsible for overall customer service standards, scheduling staff, financial accountability and accounting for on hand cash, waiting list procedures, child care enrollment procedures, room counts/attendance reports, and United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) reporting. The incumbent recommends to the CDC Director innovation/policy changes or refining methods and techniques to be used in providing and continually improving the CYP. In the absence of the CDC Director, the incumbent assumes responsibilities and performs duties and requirements of the position under higher level supervision with oversight. The incumbent is expected to apply subject knowledge, ensure policy compliance, and use initiative and creativity in accomplishing plans, outcomes, goals, and objectives. The success of the CYP requires ongoing interpretation of program policies, professional development of CYP employees, and needs of children, youth, and parents. The work includes numerous and unrelated processes and procedures concerning the wide variety of activities in a CYP. The incumbent serves as a mandated reporter as prescribed by local policy in the case of suspected incidences of child abuse and neglect. The incumbent has knowledge of Federal, State and local laws governing the detection, prevention, and reporting of child abuse and/or neglect.MAJOR DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIESProgram ManagementAssists with providing program oversight and accountability for the performance of employees, the safety of children, and customer needs. Assists with the collection and maintenance of up-to-date statistical data for planning and reporting purposes for higher headquarters and statutory requirements and to maximize spaces and ensure that resources accommodate the needs of command personnel. Assists with the development, implementation and analysis of surveys and needs assessments of staff and patrons to ensure appropriate programming and hours of operation. Incumbent must have the ability to use Microsoft Office Suite.Financial and Facility Management Operates program in compliance with internal control standards. Assists with the preparation and execution of Appropriated fund (APF) and Nonappropriated fund (NAF) budgets. Conducts written analysis of budget variances as necessary. Assists with the development of capital budget to include facility sustainment, restoration, renovation and maintenance; equipment; furniture and fixture life cycle replacement; and curriculum updates. Assists in managing the purchases of supplies, travel, training, contracted services, and capital expenditures. Tracks and analyzes income and expenditures and assures accounting of all funds and assets. Assists with the collection, accurate accounting, and reporting of funds received from patrons. Ensures staff is properly trained in cash handling procedures to include collecting, recording and deposition all fees/charges. Ensures standards are maintained for facility condition, safety and sanitation. Manages indoor/outdoor spaces to meet fire, safety and health requirements. Personnel Management Initiates and tracks work requests, coordinating and seeking approval for facility needs from routine maintenance to major renovation or construction. Interfaces routinely with the support proponent(s) for facility maintenance, repair, and modernization and provides oversight of routine maintenance and renovation. Applications submitted here are actively reviewed by Program Directors, Coordinators, and/or members of site hiring teams across our school-based afterschool sites in Brooklyn, the Bronx, and Manhattan.(If you are looking for roles within our Residencies or Signature Programs, please check our main careers page for those separate listings, as they require distinct qualifications).To be considered for our Afterschool positions, you must complete the brief location and role questionnaire attached to this application.💫 Who We AreLearning through an Expanded Arts Program (LEAP) is a collective of bold, passionate, and curious humans who believe in the power of the arts and the power of young people. We’re dreamers and doers. Visionaries and teammates. We laugh, we collaborate, we grow together—because at the heart of our work is a commitment to community and connection.Our Culture is Our Canvas:🎯 Our Goals: We collaborate with purpose and hold ourselves accountable. We reflect, learn, and celebrate big and small wins.🧑🏽‍🤝‍🧑🏽 Our Peers: We listen deeply, communicate clearly, and support each other with compassion. Feedback is a gift—and we give and receive it with care.🏛 Our Space: We show up honestly, trust each other boldly, and respect each other’s needs. We strive to create spaces that feel safe, empowering, and joyful.🌎 Our Community: We are inclusive by design and equity-driven by nature. We amplify the voices of youth and honor the diversity of the communities we serve.💼 Core Afterschool Roles & Hourly Pay Ranges:Hourly rates within each range are commensurate with experience.🧩 Teaching Artist ($30.00 - $50.00 / hour): Experienced classroom creatives who design and lead culturally responsive, art-focused workshops that integrate arts and academic learning to spark youth creativity and self-expression.🍎 Activity Specialist ($22.00 - $30.00 / hour): Creative lead instructors who design and facilitate hands-on, specialized clubs (such as STEM, chess, culinary arts, fashion, or athletics) that fuse arts with academic learning.📦 Group Leader ($18.00 - $21.00 / hour): Reliable and energetic mentors who model positive behavior, ensure participant safety, and support daily program operations by helping to facilitate academically aligned arts, sports, or STEM instruction.Whether you’re a classroom magician, a sports superhero, or a fine arts specialist—there’s a place for you here in our afterschool community.Explore our website to learn more about our impact: leapnyc.orgLet’s create something beautiful together. 💜Note: A minimum of a High School diploma or its equivalent is required upon hire. Candidates must also be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for visa sponsorship.PRE-EMPLOYMENT SCREENINGPre-employment screening is required for this position, including but not limited to criminal history checks by regulating agencies as needed per placement. WE ARE AN EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYERPlease note: In accordance with organizational policy, LEAP does not sponsor individuals on O-1 visas.

enrollment.Monitor and ensure that daily attendance, health checks, parent sign/scan in, and meal participation reports are completed daily.Maintain timely and effective communication through daily CPR and First Aid certification, and Food Handlers certification. Additional training requirements include Mandated Reporter, Health and Safety Basics, Sudden Infant Death Syndrome, and Shaken Baby Syndrome.Administer medication as needed (ex. childhood programFlexibility to work a schedule between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.Proficiency with basic computer applications and adaptability to learn and effectively use new technology and software programs as needed.Strong communication and interpersonal skills when working with diverse families, children, and professionals.Sound judgment and discretion when handling confidential information and materials.Respectful and responsive communication that demonstrates care, professionalism, and concern for others.A collaborative and supportive approach to working effectively as a member of a team.Understanding of Early Head Start, Head Start, and other developmentally appropriate early childhood programs, including the application of program practices and requirements.Knowledge and application of child development and early childhood principles, practices, and curricula appropriate to the assigned age group (birth–3 or 3–5 years).Physical RequirementsCapacity to safely lift and carry up to 40 pounds as required by the position.Comfort and physical mobility to participate in classroom activities at children's level, including jobs.title: Case Manager - Crestview Mobile Response Team at LifeView Group
jobs.description: Employer: LifeView Group - Lakeview Center Inc. Expires: 11/26/2026 Lakeview Center provides comprehensive behavioral health care to adults and children with mental illnesses, drug and alcohol dependencies and intellectual disabilities. Across Northwest Florida, our services range from residential treatment to outpatient counseling, psychiatry, trauma care, treatments for substance misuse and 24/7 support for those with serious mental illnesses. Learn more at eLakeviewCenter.org.About LCI with BenefitsMedical • Dental • Vision • Basic Life and AD&D • Voluntary Term Life • Employer Paid Long Term Disability • Flexible Spending Accounts and Health Savings Account • Retirement Savings Plan (RSP) • Employee Assistance Program • Accident Insurance • Group Critical Illness Insurance • Individual Short-Term Disability Insurance • Paid Time Off • Identity Theft Protection • Employee Discount Program • Teladoc Mobile Response Team (MRT) - Lakeview Center also has an emergency community option. The MRT serves residents of Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa and Walton counties. They provide 24/7 intervention and support for individuals in crisis via telephone triage or in-person. MRT comes to you seeking to: • Reduce trauma. • Prevent unnecessary hospitalizations. • Divert persons from juvenile or criminal system.Overview:The purpose of case management is to assist clients in gaining access to needed medical, social, educational, and other services. The primary goal of case management is to optimize the functioning of individuals who have complex needs by coordinating the provision of quality treatment and support services in the most efficient and effective manner. The desired outcomes for persons using the service system are self-sufficiency, and satisfaction in the living, learning, work and social environments of their choice.Role Requirements:Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university or college with a major in counseling, social work, psychology, criminal justice, nursing, rehabilitation, special education, health education, or a related human services field (a related human services field is one in which major course work includes the study of human behavior and development).Must have a minimum of one (1) year of full time or equivalent experience working with: adults experiencing serious mental illness.ORBachelor’s degree from an accredited university or college and three (3) years full time or equivalent experience working with: adults experiencing serious mental illness.Must be able to travel locally to clients’ homes, training locations and other locations as necessary. Ability to complete approved mental health targeted case management training within three months of initially providing case management services.Must have knowledge of available resources in the service area for adults with serious mental illness.Must have knowledge of and comply with state and federal statutes, rules and policies that effect the target population.Must be able to provide individualized, integrated mental health, substance abuse and co- occurring services to meet the needs of individuals served and their families. Must be able to use a computer.Good oral and written communication skills.Ability to work within the guidelines established in the policies and procedures of the agency and program.Ability to work cooperatively and collaboratively with multidisciplinary staff.Ability to recognize signs and symptoms of abuse. Ability to effectively relate to a variety of individuals, including persons living with a mental illness and/or substance use disorder, persons with developmental disabilities, family members of persons served, and co-workers.Ability to problem solve and advocate for persons served.Ability to assist in maintaining a therapeutic milieu.Ability to provide in home and in community services.Must be able to pass organization screening requirements, including state or federal background screenings as appropriate.Must possess a valid driver’s license from the state in which you reside, a good driving record and be insurable under the corporate policy. CompensationBase pay ranges from $20.2255 to $21.8558 an hour with an additional supplemental pay (up to 10% of base pay) for Mobile Response Team members. To Apply:Interested applicants please visit https://www.lifeviewgroup.org/careers-overview and complete the on-line application. If you require additional assistance, please call Human Resources at 850-495-3512.LifeView Group, Inc.is an Equal Opportunity employer. Individuals with Disabilities and Veterans are encouraged to apply. Drug Free Workplace Employer, DRUG TESTING REQUIRED.A Level II background screening is required. For more information, please use the following link. HB531 | Florida Agency for Health Care Administration

jobs.description: Employer: Inspired Play Learning Center Expires: 11/26/2026 Preschool Lead Teacher — Little Canada, Minnesota | On-Site | Full-TimeAbout Inspired Play Learning Center Inspired Play Learning Center is a boutique early childhood program rooted in calm, intentional environments where children learn through exploration, independence, and meaningful connection. Our approach blends play-based learning with Montessori-inspired principles, emphasizing hands-on discovery, thoughtfully prepared environments, and respect for the child.We are seeking a warm, reflective, and organized Preschool Lead Teacher who values child-led learning and believes children thrive when given beauty, structure, freedom within limits, and purposeful work.Our Preschool Lead Teachers thoughtfully guide children through a balanced day of inquiry, independence, collaboration, and exploration. Teachers serve as calm facilitators and observers, carefully preparing the environment to foster curiosity, concentration, confidence, and intrinsic motivation. This role is ideal for an educator who appreciates Montessori-inspired philosophy while working within a collaborative, relationship-centered preschool setting.Key ResponsibilitiesPrepared Environment & Child-Led Learning- Create and maintain a peaceful, organized classroom with intentionally designed learning areas - Guide children through hands-on, inquiry-based experiences rooted in practical life, early literacy, math, science, sensory exploration, and creative expression - Foster independence, problem-solving, concentration, and self-regulation through thoughtful classroom routines and guidance - Observe children closely to inform individualized learning opportunities and classroom planning - Support freedom within limits while maintaining a calm, respectful classroom culture Relationships & Communication - Build trusting partnerships with children, families, and colleagues - Communicate professionally and warmly with families regarding children's development and daily experiences - Collaborate with co-teachers and support staff to maintain consistency and flow throughout the day Professional Responsibilities - Maintain accurate observations and developmental documentation - Uphold all licensing, health, and safety standards - Participate in ongoing professional growth and reflective practice - Contribute positively to a calm, collaborative team culture Who You Are You are: - Calm, patient, and emotionally attuned - Organized and intentional in your classroom practices - Respectful of children's autonomy and developmental pace - Passionate about hands-on, child-centered learning - Able to balance structure with flexibility and curiosityYou believe the environment acts as a teacher, and that meaningful learning happens through purposeful exploration and connection. Qualifications - Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Early Childhood Education or related field preferred - Montessori training or Montessori-inspired classroom experience strongly valued - Experience working with preschool-aged children in a licensed setting - Strong understanding of child development and child-led learning practices - Excellent communication, classroom leadership, and collaboration skills - CPR/First Aid certified or willing to obtain - Meets all Minnesota licensing requirements Physical Requirements This is an active teaching role requiring full engagement with young children throughout the day, including: - Sitting on the floor, bending, kneeling, and frequent movement - Lifting and assisting children (up to 40 lbs) - Engaging in active indoor and outdoor play - Supporting children with daily care routines as needed - Maintaining awareness and responsiveness within a dynamic classroom environment Why Join Inspired Play Learning Center? - Small classrooms and low ratios - Calm, beautifully organized learning environments - Supportive leadership and collaborative culture - Opportunity to help shape a growing Montessori-inspired program - Paid professional development and growth opportunities Join a center where children are respected, curiosity is nurtured, and play has purpose.

jobs.description: Employer: KinderCare Learning Companies Expires: 11/26/2026 Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. jobs.title: Whitefish High School - School Psychologist (.5 FTE) at Whitefish School District
jobs.description: Employer: Whitefish School District Expires: 11/26/2026 POSITION TITLE: School Psychologist REPORTS TO: Director of Student Services / Building Principal POSITION SUMMARY Provide a full range of school psychological and psycho-educational services to support the academic, behavioral, and social-emotional competence of students ages 3-18 across one or more sites within the Whitefish School District. Whitefish Public Schools seeks educators with a track record of raising student achievement to join a team dedicated to providing a deeper learning instructional program, utilizing data to drive daily practice, and supporting an inclusive school culture. It is the expectation of the District that each staff member will put the safety, health, and well-being of students at the forefront of all actions, job responsibilities, and decisions and perform all duties in alignment with the District’s Strategic Plan. POSITION QUALIFICATIONS Minimum Qualifications: Education: M.A., M.S., Ed.S., or Ph.D. in School Psychology from an accredited institution. Licensure/Certification: Valid Class 6 Specialist Certificate with a School Psychologist endorsement from the Montana Office of Public Instruction (or immediate eligibility for certification). Communication Skills: Demonstrated ability to write reports and business correspondence; ability to communicate clearly, concisely, and effectively in writing and orally to students, staff, parents, and the general public. Professional Relations: Proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with students, peers, parents, and the broader community. Operational Capacity: Ability to effectively manage time and responsibilities, interpret oral/written instructions, and maintain student confidentiality. Preferred Qualifications: Advanced training and/or verified field experience working within established Response to Intervention (RTI) and MTSS frameworks. JOB RESPONSIBILITIES & ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS (including but not limited to):: 1. Assessment, Evaluation, & Case Management: Administer, score, and analyze a variety of psycho-educational evaluations and supplemental assessments relevant to individual student needs. Identify and assess the learning, development, adjustment, functional capabilities, and environmental factors affecting student performance. Conduct Functional Behavioral Assessments (FBAs) and develop Behavior Intervention Plans (BIPs). Conduct Threat Assessments as needed to ensure campus safety. Actively assist and participate in Child Find testing and screening activities. 2. Consultation, Collaboration, & Team Participation: Participate in the Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS) and Response to Intervention (RTI) processes, utilizing and communicating Curriculum-Based Measurement (CBM) data and progress monitoring tools. Participate in multi-disciplinary referral and Special Education meetings to help determine appropriate student placement and contribute to the development of Individualized Education Programs (IEPs). Participate in Student Assistance Teams to collaborate on targeted pre-referral interventions. Consult with school staff, administration, and parents regarding learning styles, classroom management, student behavior modifications, and school-wide needs to enhance student achievement. Provide confidential information to teachers or principals when it is deemed to be in the student’s best educational and personal interests. 3. Intervention & Student/Parent Support: Develop, implement, and monitor individual, group, or system-level interventions addressing academic, social-emotional, behavioral, and mental health needs. As directed by the Student Services Director, and in concert with School Counselors, provide shortterm individual and group counseling services for students. As directed by the Student Services Director, and in concert with School Counselors, counsel parents regarding effective strategies to manage their child's specific behavioral, emotional, and learning needs, and make recommendations to outside counseling resources when necessary. Participate in vocational and transitional planning for special education students. Assist in the development, implementation, and training of building-wide programs that support student behavioral and academic success. 4. Data Systems, Professional Growth, & Administration: Document and maintain rigorous records of parent contact, counseling sessions, and classroom interventions. Support the design and implementation of data collection systems to facilitate data-based decision making. Adhere to and maintain knowledge of state and federal rules, regulations, district policies, and professional ethics/standards of school psychology (including student confidentiality). Engage in continuous professional development, peer collaboration, research application, and staff development opportunities. Perform other duties and functions as required, given, or assigned by the Director of Student Services or Building Principal.

Clear Communication: Notify administrative staff promptly of any schedule changes, cancellations, or technical issues affecting lessons. Incident Documentation: Maintain thorough records of any incidents or technical disruptions affecting student engagement or lesson delivery. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills to build trust with children and families. Reliable transportation and willingness to travel to students’ homes. Ability to manage a flexible schedule, including occasional evenings or weekends. Must be available and open to working at least 20 hours per week. Bi-lingual in Spanish(a plus but not required) Candidates must be willing to undergo a background check as part of the hiring process.Please note that because this position involves driving and working with vulnerable populations, information obtained through the background check process may be considered when evaluating a candidate's suitability. If you have questions, contact the Recruiting Manager at eparedes@arabesqueconservatory.com What We Offer: Competitive hourly pay for teaching time, plus paid driving time and mileage reimbursement. Flexible part-time hours to accommodate your schedule. Opportunities for professional development and growth within the United Academy of Music & Arts. A supportive team environment committed to inclusive and adaptive music education. DD Specialists must also maintain clear and accurate documentation, utilizing electronic platforms, in accordance with county and state rules.Depending on assignment, more specific duties may include:Completing the Oregon Needs Assessment (ONA) through document review, face-to-face contact and an interview process with the individual, family/guardian, service providers and other supports. jobs.title: Youth Program Manager at Operation HOPE-North County
jobs.description: Employer: Operation HOPE-North County Expires: 11/26/2026 Operation HOPE-North County Youth Program Manager Position: Youth Program Manager Location: Vista, California Employment Type: Part-Time, Non-Exempt Schedule: Monday–Friday, 4:30 PM–9:00 PM (22.5 hours per week) Compensation: 20–25 per hour, depending on qualifications and experience Reports To: Shelter ManagerAbout Operation HOPE-North County Operation HOPE-North County is a nonprofit organization dedicated to providing a safe, supportive environment for families with children and single women experiencing homelessness as they work toward stability, self-sufficiency, and lasting independence. Our year-round shelter provides more than a safe place to sleep. Through compassionate case management, educational enrichment, life skills development, and community partnerships, we help families overcome barriers and build brighter futures. We believe every child deserves the opportunity to learn, grow, play, and thrive, regardless of their family's circumstances. Position Summary Operation HOPE-North County is seeking a compassionate, creative, organized, and enthusiastic Youth Program Manager to lead and strengthen our HOPE for Kids youth enrichment program. The Youth Program Manager is responsible for the planning, coordination, daily implementation, and evaluation of engaging, structured, and developmentally appropriate programming for children and youth residing in our shelter. This is a hands-on leadership position requiring strong organizational skills, creativity, initiative, and the ability to effectively coordinate children, volunteers, and support staff in a dynamic shelter environment. The Youth Program Manager will ensure that every program session is thoughtfully planned, adequately staffed, safe, and engaging, with clear activities and learning opportunities for children of different ages and developmental stages. The ideal candidate is passionate about youth development, understands the impact of trauma and housing instability on children and families, and has demonstrated experience developing enrichment activities, leading volunteers, and managing daily program operations. Key Responsibilities Youth Program Development and Implementation Plan, coordinate, and facilitate engaging youth enrichment activities that support academic, social, emotional, physical, and creative development. Lead the HOPE for Kids program, incorporating educational enrichment, arts and crafts, recreation, wellness, life skills, and social-emotional learning. Develop monthly program calendars and detailed weekly lesson plans that reflect the interests, developmental needs, and abilities of participating children. Design and implement structured, age-appropriate activities for two primary groups: younger children (ages 0–6) and older children (ages 7+). Coordinate simultaneous activities for both age groups, ensuring each receives meaningful engagement, appropriate supervision, and a consistent program experience. Facilitate structured indoor and outdoor activities that promote positive peer relationships, confidence, creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving. Incorporate intentional, play-based learning and recreational activities rather than relying on extended periods of unstructured free play. Adapt programming to accommodate changing attendance, developmental differences, individual support needs, and shelter enrollment. Create opportunities for children to experience joy, belonging, stability, and personal growth. Ensure activities are inclusive, culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and accessible to children of varying ages and abilities. Curriculum Development and Lesson Planning Develop and submit detailed weekly lesson plans in advance, according to established organizational deadlines. Ensure every lesson plan includes: Clear learning or developmental objectives. Detailed activity descriptions and intended outcomes. Step-by-step instructions for introducing, facilitating, and concluding each activity. A breakdown of the time allocated to each activity component. Required materials, supplies, and preparation instructions. Specific staff and volunteer responsibilities. Age-appropriate modifications and alternative activities. Develop lesson plans detailed enough that another staff member or volunteer can independently facilitate activities when needed. Ensure activities are intentionally designed to engage children throughout scheduled program periods. Prepare additional activities or extensions for children who complete activities early. Organize, prepare, and clearly label materials and supplies before scheduled activities. Identify and communicate supply needs in advance to ensure program readiness. Regularly evaluate activities and incorporate feedback to improve engagement and program quality. Daily Youth Program Operations and Leadership Oversee the daily operation of HOPE for Kids, ensuring that programming begins on time and follows an organized, consistent schedule. Develop and implement daily program agendas identifying activities, locations, assigned personnel, and transitions. Lead daily opening huddles with children, staff, and volunteers to review introductions, activities, expectations, and responsibilities. Coordinate transitions between activity areas and age groups, ensuring children remain appropriately supervised. Ensure staff and volunteers understand the day's lesson plans and are prepared to facilitate their assigned activities. Maintain organized, welcoming, and safe indoor and outdoor program environments. Conduct brief daily debriefs with staff and volunteers to discuss successes, challenges, and opportunities for improvement. Demonstrate strong leadership, sound judgment, initiative, and proactive problem-solving. Maintain continuity of programming by ensuring schedules, materials, and lesson plans are accessible to designated staff in the event of an absence. Volunteer Leadership and Community Partner Coordination Coordinate daily volunteer check-in, orientation, assignments, and engagement. Welcome new volunteers and introduce them to children, families, staff, and other volunteers as appropriate. Ensure every volunteer receives a clear assignment and understands their specific responsibilities. Provide volunteers with detailed instructions and guidance for facilitating activities and supporting children. Actively monitor volunteer engagement and provide redirection, coaching, and support as needed. Delegate appropriate responsibilities for activity preparation, facilitation, supervision support, transitions, and cleanup. Ensure volunteers follow organizational policies related to child safety, confidentiality, and professional boundaries. Coordinate guest instructors, educational workshops, recreational activities, and special events. Develop and maintain relationships with schools, nonprofits, businesses, and community organizations to expand enrichment opportunities. Identify opportunities for donated supplies, educational materials, and program resources. Foster a positive, collaborative environment that encourages meaningful volunteer participation and retention. Youth Engagement and Positive Behavior Support Build positive, trusting, and supportive relationships with children and families residing at the shelter. Foster a welcoming environment where children feel emotionally and physically safe, respected, included, and valued. Establish clear, consistent, and developmentally appropriate behavioral expectations. Develop and implement positive reinforcement strategies that encourage kindness, cooperation, participation, responsibility, and respectful behavior. Model healthy communication, emotional regulation, and effective conflict-resolution skills. Use trauma-informed, strengths-based approaches when responding to behavioral or emotional challenges. Support children in developing social-emotional skills, confidence, independence, and healthy peer relationships. Recognize and accommodate the individual developmental, emotional, and behavioral needs of participating children. Collaborate with shelter staff and case managers to identify opportunities to better support children's educational and developmental needs. Maintain appropriate professional boundaries and ensure all children are treated with dignity, compassion, and respect. Child Safety and Active Supervision Maintain active oversight of all participating children and ensure appropriate supervision across all program areas. Ensure younger children receive the same level of intentional engagement, attention, and support as older children. Establish clear supervision assignments for indoor activities, outdoor recreation, transitions, and other program components. Maintain accurate attendance records and account for participating children throughout each session. Follow established procedures for child check-in, authorized release, and parent or caregiver communication. Ensure program activities, materials, and equipment are safe and developmentally appropriate. Monitor program spaces for potential hazards and address safety concerns promptly. Follow organizational policies related to mandated reporting, confidentiality, emergency procedures, incident documentation, and child safeguarding. Respond appropriately to injuries, behavioral incidents, or safety concerns and communicate them promptly through established organizational channels. Collaborate with shelter staff to ensure adequate supervision and continuity of care. Program Administration, Documentation, and Evaluation Maintain accurate daily youth attendance records, activity logs, program sheets, calendars, and participation data. Complete required daily program documentation and submit reports according to established organizational deadlines. Track program outputs and outcomes, including classes delivered, attendance, participation, and youth engagement. Maintain organized program records that support continuity, accountability, and program evaluation. Collect feedback from children, parents, volunteers, and staff to continuously improve programming. Assist with gathering program stories, impact data, and information for grant reports and donor communications, while protecting client confidentiality. Manage youth program supplies, inventory, and expenditures within an approved budget. Communicate staffing gaps, program challenges, supply needs, and safety concerns proactively. Provide regular program updates to organizational leadership. Support the development of program goals, evaluation tools, and continuous quality improvement strategies. 8. Program Space Organization and Readiness Ensure all program areas are clean, organized, welcoming, and ready for daily activities. Prepare activity materials, supplies, and equipment before children arrive. Maintain clearly organized and labeled storage systems for program supplies. Assign appropriate setup and cleanup responsibilities to volunteers and support staff. Encourage children to participate in age-appropriate cleanup activities. Ensure program materials are properly stored and activity spaces are restored at the conclusion of each session. Maintain a consistent standard of program readiness and organization. Collaboration and Organizational Leadership Collaborate closely with shelter staff, case managers, volunteers, and organizational leadership to support the needs of children and families. Communicate effectively and professionally with parents, caregivers, colleagues, and community partners. Participate in staff meetings, professional development opportunities, and organizational events as needed. Demonstrate reliability, initiative, accountability, and the ability to work independently. Identify opportunities to strengthen program quality, efficiency, youth engagement, and volunteer participation. Support the mission, values, policies, and overall goals of Operation HOPE-North County. Qualifications Required Experience working directly with children or youth in educational, recreational, nonprofit, community-based, or social service settings. Demonstrated ability to develop structured lesson plans and facilitate engaging, age-appropriate enrichment activities. Experience coordinating or leading volunteers, support staff, or group activities. Strong organizational, time-management, and program coordination skills. Ability to manage simultaneous activities, changing attendance, and multiple age groups. Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills. Ability to provide clear instructions, delegate responsibilities, and guide volunteers effectively. Ability to build positive relationships with children, parents, volunteers, and colleagues. Understanding of, or willingness to learn, trauma-informed care and the challenges associated with family homelessness. Ability to work independently, demonstrate initiative, and adapt to changing program needs. Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and culturally responsive programming. Availability to work the required Monday–Friday afternoon and evening schedule. Ability to satisfy applicable background screening and child safety requirements. CPR and First Aid certification, or ability to obtain certification within a timeframe established by the organization. Preferred Qualifications Associate's or bachelor's degree in Child Development, Education, Social Work, Psychology, Human Services, Recreation, or a related field. Two or more years of experience in youth development, after-school programming, education, or community-based services. Experience working with children and families experiencing homelessness, poverty, trauma, or housing instability. Experience developing curriculum, structured activities, or enrichment programming for multiple age groups. Knowledge of social-emotional learning, positive youth development, and restorative practices. Experience coordinating volunteers, supervising program activities, or developing community partnerships. Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish. Core Competencies The successful candidate will demonstrate: Compassion and Empathy: A genuine commitment to supporting children and families experiencing difficult circumstances. Creativity and Initiative: The ability to independently design meaningful, engaging, and developmentally appropriate activities. Organization and Preparation: Strong attention to detail, advance planning, and consistent program readiness. Leadership and Accountability: The ability to coordinate volunteers and support staff, communicate expectations, and take ownership of daily program operations. Trauma-Informed Practice: An understanding of how adversity can affect children's behavior, development, and sense of safety. Positive Youth Engagement: The ability to create supportive, inclusive environments that encourage participation and healthy relationships. Communication and Collaboration: Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively with families, volunteers, colleagues, and community partners. Adaptability and Problem-Solving: The ability to respond thoughtfully and effectively to changing needs in a dynamic shelter environment. Program Goals and Performance Expectations The Youth Program Manager will contribute to the following organizational priorities: Support the delivery of approximately 280 youth enrichment classes annually, across four program categories. Maintain a consistent, engaging, and developmentally appropriate youth activity calendar. Ensure timely preparation and submission of complete weekly lesson plans and daily program schedules. Maintain structured, age-appropriate programming for both younger and older children. Ensure volunteers receive consistent orientation, clear assignments, and appropriate support. Maintain a safe, organized, and welcoming program environment. Increase meaningful participation and engagement in HOPE for Kids programming. Strengthen relationships with community partners and volunteer instructors. Maintain accurate attendance, activity, and program outcome documentation. Incorporate youth and family feedback into program improvement. Support the organization's ability to demonstrate measurable impact to funders and community stakeholders. Annual goals will be adjusted to reflect staffing capacity, program resources, and organizational priorities. Work Environment and Physical Requirements This position is based primarily onsite at Operation HOPE-North County's shelter in Vista, California. Responsibilities involve direct interaction with children and families, facilitating indoor and outdoor activities, preparing program spaces, and participating in recreational and educational programming. The position may require standing, walking, bending, and lifting program supplies of up to 25 pounds, with reasonable accommodations available in accordance with applicable law. Equal Employment Opportunity Operation HOPE-North County is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds who share our commitment to serving families and children with dignity, compassion, and respect. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit a resume and brief cover letter describing their experience working with children, developing enrichment programming, and their interest in supporting youth experiencing homelessness. esperanza@operationhopeshelter.org Join us in helping children build confidence, discover their strengths, and experience the stability, connection, and opportunity every child deserves.

jobs.description: Employer: Camp Augusta Expires: 11/26/2026 Camp Counselor- Leadership Track Opportunity Location: Northern California, United States (On-site housing provided)Position Type: Full-time, seasonal (May 18th-August 14th)Compensation: From $4500 + housing, utilities, organic meals, and professional mobility Make a Difference and Grow Your Skills for the FutureAre you passionate about youth development and looking for an impactful summer that doubles as a launchpad for your career? Camp Augusta offers a transformative experience where counselors are guides, mentors, and leaders who make a lasting difference in campers' lives; this role integrates especially well with those looking to grow professionally on a path in youth development, education, therapy, social work, or leadership roles. Beyond just a summer job, we invest deeply in your growth and offer individual training in the summer with the intention that you'd return the following summer in a leadership role. Why Choose Camp Augusta?Camp Augusta isn’t your average summer camp—here’s what makes us different:Unmatched Training: Begin with over 300 hours of in-depth training covering child development, emotional intelligence, and group dynamics. You’ll gain real tools for working with youth and teams in any future career.Structured Leadership Path: Counselors who shine have the opportunity to move up through various leadership roles in areas like program management, logistics, and staff support in future summers.Dynamic Programming: With 150+ activities (from archery to circus arts), no two days are alike. You’ll lead, teach, and innovate, all while building versatile skills.Human-Centered Approach: Grounded in Rational-Emotive Behavior Therapy and Nonviolent Communication, our program empowers campers and staff alike to grow through empathy, self-expression, and resilience. Your Role as a Camp Counselor (This Summer)As a Camp Counselor, you’ll be responsible for a cabin of 5 campers at a time, creating a safe, fun, and empowering environment that allows them to explore, grow, and make lasting memories. After completing our comprehensive training program, you’ll put your skills to use each day, leading activities, guiding campers, and contributing to the overall camp magic.Your Day at Camp Augusta will look like this:Creating Special Wake-Ups: Create a memorable and intentional Special Wake-Up for your cabin, setting the tone for a fun and meaningful day.Facilitating a Robust Variety of Clinics: Lead four different activity blocks each day from the wide array of activities you’ll choose to focus on during training. From circus arts to archery to crafts—your day is varied, creative, and full of new learning.Designing Cabin Activities: Lead your cabin in daily activities that promote teamwork, creativity, and self-expression, such as art projects, skits, or nature walks.Evening Programs: Be part of our evening programs, where you’ll play in large-scale games like capture the flag, or take on roles in immersive, creative camp-wide events. You’ll help make these programs unforgettable for campers through skits, songs, and your best character performances.Evening Embers: End each day with thoughtful, silly, and memorable activities (Embers) to help campers connect, reflect, and prepare for the days ahead.Give back with heart: Gift your campers two personal gifts each session: a hand-crafted wood cookie and a heartfelt Parent Letter, showing your investment in their growth and journey.Counselors are the heartbeat of camp, and our words are critical to bringing our hearts to theirs. Most counselors spend a session or two outside of the cabin as well, contributing to programming or other areas of interest. See our page on counselor life for more information on the role and how it differs from most other camps. Leadership Development - The Augusta Growth Track (This Summer and Beyond!)At Camp Augusta, we believe in investing in our counselors not just for the summer, but for the future. Our structured Leadership Track allows high-performing counselors to gain hands-on experience in program management, staff support, and logistics, preparing you for future roles within and beyond the camp. This generally looks like spending 3 weeks of the summer our of the cabin with an emphasis in participating and training in another domain.Leadership tracks offer in-summer training for the roles of:Master of Fun & Games: Have a flair for our epic games and activities? Work on logistics, staging, and game oversight, collaborating with our MFG team to run unforgettable camp programs.Village Leadership: Ready for a ‘cabin’ of young adults for a summer? Support fellow counselors alongside our Village Leaders, gaining experience in team management, parent communication, and more.Area Program Directors: Take the lead in domains with our Arts Directors, Challenge Course Managers, Equestrian Team, or Masters of Fun and Games.Office & Administration: Passionate about keeping camp running? Explore camp logistics behind the scenes, with roles in scheduling, holistic management, and programming coordination.More Specialized Areas!: Check out all of our non-counseling roles and identify the one you're most interested in. If your strengths match the role, we'll get you involved and trained.These experiences provide invaluable skills for careers in youth development, social work, education, counseling, and beyond. Who We’re Looking For:We seek energetic, passionate individuals eager to work with kids and committed to personal growth. You don’t need all the answers from day one; we’re here to mentor and support you.Minimum Requirements:Must be 19 or older by June 1st, 2027.Available for full summer: May 18th to August 14th, 2026 (includes 3.5 weeks of training and 9 weeks of summer camp).Ability to commit to ~5 hours/week of pre-camp onboarding fro the date you're hired till you arrive (depending on hire date)A strong desire to grow into a leadership position, with a commitment to returning for subsequent summers.AND MUST have two of the following: At least one summer of experience at a summer campOver 100 hours of direct professional (paid) mentorship work with youthA major or background directly related to working with youth, with the intention to work with youth in your future career Preferred Qualifications:Experience working with children in a meaningful way (e.g., previous camp, childcare, or mentorship experience)A passion for personal development and the ability to apply your learning to your work with campers. What You'll Receive:Competitive Compensation: $4500 for the summerFull Housing & Meals: Enjoy our on-site lodging and healthy, organic mealsComprehensive Training: Gain 300+ hours of training plus ongoing mentorship and leadership developmentAn Inspiring Community: Join a team of dedicated individuals who are as passionate about growth and impact as you are Internships?Yup, we do that. We can co-design your internship based on the skills and development you seek, and the specific requirements of your school!Note: Some educational institutions require prior approval before the start of an internship. It is the responsibility of the student to check with their institution to be sure they meet any requirements before they accept a position.If you have internship requirements, we can almost definitely meet them! About Camp Augusta:Camp Augusta is a nonprofit residential summer camp in northern California that offers a truly unique summer camp experience for campers and staff alike. We are focused on counseling skills, creativity, excellent programming, and camper choice - see more about the vision of our camp here.We aim to include and celebrate many facets of human identity – gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, race, age, neurodiversity, disability status, citizenship, and other aspects that make us unique. We are working to craft an inclusive culture founded on ideals of curiosity, honesty, empathy, and acceptance – a place where people are seen and acknowledged for their shared humanity as well as their unique individuality. Read our full Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, And Belonging (DEIB) Statement here. Do you have any questions?Send us a message on Handshake, and we'll get back to you by the end of the next day! You can also send any questions you have to applications@campaugusta.org.Feeling ready to apply?1. Take 5 minutes to fill out our interest form. 2. Someone from our hiring team will reach out to you within 24 hours.3. Schedule an Intro Chat with us, and complete a full application!
